waypoints.name: Sargans fuel gate
waypoints.advice: Sargans is where the day begins. Next is Bludenz food stop.

waypoints.name: Bludenz food stop
waypoints.advice: Bludenz food stop is where this day stops to eat. Next is Arlberg return option, climbing 1205 m.

waypoints.name: Arlberg return option
waypoints.advice: The route ends here after 143 km. The road climbs 1205 m on the way up to it, steadily. Reckon on about 9 °C colder than the valley, and more in the wind. Nothing on this route is higher.

Bludenz food stop → Arlberg return option climbs about 1205 m in 37 km. This is the part worth slowing down for - look through the bends and use the pull-offs.

scenicChapters.title: Grand Tour of Switzerland
scenicChapters.narrative: For 72 km this is Grand Tour of Switzerland, a road with a name of its own and a reason for it — expect company on a summer weekend. Early is better than fast.

scenicChapters.title: Silvretta High Alpine Road
scenicChapters.narrative: The last of the trees go and the road runs out onto open ground. The summit sits at 1793 m, and what surrounds it is rock, weather and distance. Cold comes early up here and stays late. Ride it with something in reserve: the summit is not the end of the work, only the middle of it.
scenicChapters.riderNote: Check the pass is open before you commit to it.

silvretta-montafon-overnight-gateway-par.story: A 143 km one-way ride from near Sargans, about 2 h 44 of riding. The highest point is 1,793 m. Arlberg Pass is subject to seasonal closure - check it is open before you set off. It crosses from Switzerland into Austria - carry ID and check vignette or toll rules.

scenicChapters.title: Villa Cornaro → Venice and its Lagoon
scenicChapters.narrative: Slow enough to look. The surface follows the shoreline, so the corners arrive where the water decided, not where an engineer did. Water arrives beside the road and stays for 44 km. The line follows the shore because there is nowhere else for it to go.
